meta.name: firecrawl-mcp-server
meta.description: Official Firecrawl MCP server, the context API for AI agents: search, scrape, and interact with the web, plus parse, crawl, map, Agent and Monitor, from any MCP client.

install.title: Installation
install.html:
Hosted MCP (keyless free tier)

Connect to the remote hosted server with no setup:

https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp

On the keyless free tier, scrape, search, and parse work without an API key (rate-limited). Other tools such as crawl, map, and agent still need a key.

Prefer OAuth or an API key whenever the human can sign up. It unlocks the full tool set and higher limits.

For an interactive account connection, configure your MCP client to use this server URL. This is an MCP endpoint, not a browser page; use the client's account-connection flow and do not add a second Firecrawl server entry when reconnecting:

https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth

For an API-key connection (for example, an unattended integration), keep the server URL as:

https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp

Then configure the client's secure header or secret setting with:

Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>

Never put an API key in the server URL. Never put an API key in an agent chat. Configure it directly in the client or secret manager. See the hosted MCP setup guide and the agent onboarding guide for client-specific instructions.

Naming your integration

An integration that connects over HTTP can name itself with an X-Firecrawl-Origin header, for example X-Firecrawl-Origin: my-agent. The server reports it to Firecrawl as the request origin mcp-my-agent@<server version>, in place of the client name or User-Agent it would otherwise report. Use letters, digits and dashes: each run of other characters becomes one dash, leading and trailing dashes are dropped, and the name is cut at 48 characters. Tool results are unaffected; only the origin sent to the Firecrawl API (and passed to an embedder's beforeKeylessRequest) changes.

Search-only endpoint

A fixed-scope search surface is also hosted at:

https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-search

It exposes a fixed set of twelve tools: firecrawl_search, firecrawl_developer_search, firecrawl_gov_search, the four firecrawl_research_* paper tools, the two Alexandria tools firecrawl_find_tools and firecrawl_scrape, and the enrich tools people_company_search and people_company_enrich, and the jobs tool jobs_search. Its firecrawl_search fetches no page content.

Running with npx
env FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY npx -y firecrawl-mcp
Manual Installation
npm install -g firecrawl-mcp
Running on Cursor

Configuring Cursor 🖥️ Note: Requires Cursor version 0.45.6+ For the most up-to-date configuration instructions, please refer to the official Cursor documentation on configuring MCP servers: Cursor MCP Server Configuration Guide

To configure Firecrawl MCP in Cursor v0.48.6

  1. Open Cursor Settings
  2. Go to Features > MCP Servers
  3. Click "+ Add new global MCP server"
  4. Enter the following code:
    {
  "mcpServers": {
    "firecrawl-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "firecrawl-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "YOUR-API-KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}

To configure Firecrawl MCP in Cursor v0.45.6

  1. Open Cursor Settings
  2. Go to Features > MCP Servers
  3. Click "+ Add New MCP Server"
  4. Enter the following:
    • Name: "firecrawl-mcp" (or your preferred name)
    • Type: "command"
    • Command: env FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=your-api-key npx -y firecrawl-mcp

If you are using Windows and are running into issues, try cmd /c "set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=your-api-key && npx -y firecrawl-mcp"

Replace your-api-key with your Firecrawl API key. If you don't have one yet, you can create an account and get it from https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys

After adding, refresh the MCP server list to see the new tools. The Composer Agent will automatically use Firecrawl MCP when appropriate, but you can explicitly request it by describing what you need from the web. Access the Composer via Command+L (Mac), select "Agent" next to the submit button, and enter your query.

Running on Windsurf

Add this to your ./codeium/windsurf/model_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-server-firecrawl": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "firecrawl-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
Running with Streamable HTTP Local Mode

To run the server using Streamable HTTP locally instead of the default stdio transport:

env HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER=true FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY npx -y firecrawl-mcp

Use the url: http://localhost:3000/mcp

In this mode the server only answers requests addressed to localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (on any port), plus the address in HOST when it isn't 0.0.0.0 or ::. A request whose Host header names another host, or whose Origin header names another site, gets 403, and CORS headers echo an allowed origin instead of *. GET and HEAD requests to /health are answered whatever the host, so health checks keep working, and the server logs a line naming FIRECRAWL_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS for every request it refuses. This stops web pages you visit from calling the local server through DNS rebinding or cross-origin requests and using its FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.

To reach the server under another name or address, such as a hostname behind a reverse proxy or a LAN IP, list it in FIRECRAWL_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS (comma-separated; ports are ignored). The same list decides which browser origins may call the server. A reverse proxy on the same machine can keep the default bind address:

env HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER=true FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY \
  FIRECRAWL_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=mcp.home.lan npx -y firecrawl-mcp

Clients on other machines also need the server to listen on a non-loopback address, so set HOST too. Every client that can reach the port is then served with the server's FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, so do this only on a network you trust:

env HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER=true FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY HOST=0.0.0.0 \
  FIRECRAWL_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=192.168.1.20 npx -y firecrawl-mcp

FIRECRAWL_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=* turns the check off and restores the wildcard CORS header. Only do that when something in front of the server checks hosts and origins itself.

Running with Docker

The ghcr.io/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server image runs the same server as npx -y firecrawl-mcp. Every build from main is tagged latest, v<package version> and sha-<commit sha>. v<package version> moves to the newest build of that version, so pin sha-<commit sha> (or a digest) when you need a fixed image.

stdio (the default), for MCP clients that launch the server as a command:

docker run -i --rm -e FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY ghcr.io/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server:latest

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "firecrawl-mcp": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-e", "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY", "ghcr.io/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server:latest"],
      "env": {
        "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}

Streamable HTTP, served at http://localhost:3000/mcp:

docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER=true \
  -e FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY \
  ghcr.io/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server:latest

The image sets HOST=0.0.0.0 and PORT=3000; override PORT (and the -p mapping) to listen elsewhere. The server uses the container's FIRECRAWL_API_KEY for requests that don't send their own credential, so the example publishes the port on 127.0.0.1 only; don't expose it more widely unless clients must supply their own key. Set FIRECRAWL_API_URL to use a self-hosted Firecrawl API. The container runs as the unprivileged node user. The server answers only localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] in the Host and Origin headers, so the -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 mapping works as is; to reach it under another name, set -e FIRECRAWL_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=<host> (see Streamable HTTP local mode).

features.title: Features
features.html:
• Search the web, optionally with full page content for each result
  • Search indexes for developer sources (GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and docs), US government sources, and scientific papers (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv)
  • Look up a protein's curated subcellular location and function in UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot, with the evidence and papers behind each statement
  • Scrape any URL into clean Markdown
  • Parse PDFs and documents
  • Crawl a site for content from many pages, or map it to discover its URLs
  • Interact with pages in a real browser: click, type, fill forms, and navigate dynamic pages
  • Run Agent jobs for multi-source research that returns structured data
  • Monitor pages and get notified when their content changes
  • Check current and historical Firecrawl credit usage
  • Automatic retries and rate limiting
  • Cloud and self-hosted support
  • SSE support

Play around with our MCP Server on MCP.so's playground or on Klavis AI.
